title: Ang 751–761: Suhi ashtpadis
tomorrow: what if you feel too clumsy to love well?

lines: ONE RED SHIRT, A PINK LOAD.
cards: One new red shirt goes in with the whites, and everything comes out pink. Some dyes run; some hold. Guru Nanak knew his dyes.
On ang 751, where Suhi's longer hymns begin, he says, in paraphrase: the color of kasumbh, safflower, is raw; it lasts only a few days. So which color holds?

teach.b: These are ashtpadis, longer hymns, and their singer is the soul-bride. In Gurbani the soul, whoever it belongs to, is pictured as a bride, and God as the husband she longs for.
Safflower gave a bright red-orange that didn't last.

teach.h: DYED IN THE TRUE ONE, IT HOLDS.
teach.b: Guru Nanak goes on, in paraphrase: without the Name, the bride wanders in doubt, robbed by the cheat of falsehood; but those dyed in the True One aren't born again. Listen to how physical it is.
A bride's clothes, a bright dye, the color washing out in a few days. The bride who chases the quick color loses it.

The color that holds is the one soaked in deep: love for the True One, the Name, the habit of remembering. Somewhere this week there's a wedding outfit on a hanger, bright and beautiful. The hymn doesn't sneer at it.
It just says the dye on the cloth isn't the color that lasts.

teach.h: NOT ONLY A WOMAN, NOT ONLY A WEDDING.
teach.b: And the bride in these hymns isn't only a woman, and isn't only at a wedding. She's anyone who wants to belong to the One, and is learning which colors run.

how: Suhi's ashtpadis are sung in kirtan; Sikhs read the soul-bride in them as the soul, and the husband as God.

games.q: your brother spends his savings on a flashy car to impress people at school. it does look great. what fits ang 751?
o: enjoy it with him; the hymn is about brides, not cars.
nice color, but it fades; what's he dyed in underneath?
admit it's smart: how people see you is what lasts.
games.why: Guru Nanak doesn't mock the bright dye; he says safflower lasts a few days. the color that holds is the one soaked in deep.

practice: Hold or look at a piece of colored cloth near you: a scarf, a sleeve, a cushion. Look at the color for the sit, and notice where it's still bright and where it has already faded. Then let your eyes rest, and the breath with them.
